name: Tessera Corponation Peripatetic Address Shell
description:
The Peripatetic Address Shell is a signal-routing device that continuously migrates its apparent broadcast origin across GLMZ's mesh infrastructure, making its user's communications appear to originate from hundreds of different physical nodes in rapid succession. Unlike simple spoofing tools, the PAS does not fabricate false origins — it actually routes signal traffic through a shifting chain of legitimate mesh relays, each hop authenticated by the next, creating a real and traceable path that nonetheless resolves to a different apparent source every 4.3 seconds. Tessera Corponation developed it initially for their own internal security teams, who needed to conduct field communications without creating locatable transmission signatures.

The device's proprietary 'address drift' algorithm is its defining feature — it learns the relay density and traffic load of whatever urban environment it operates in, prioritizing high-traffic nodes where an additional signal is statistically invisible and deprioritizing quiet relays where anomalous traffic might trigger automated flags. The result is a communication device that hides not by going silent, but by becoming indistinguishable from the city's own noise. Users report that in dense districts, the PAS achieves what Tessera's documentation calls 'statistical anonymity' — the probability of tracing a call drops below actionable thresholds within the first two minutes of transmission.

The Shell is physically unassuming — a matte black rectangular unit worn on the forearm or kept in a jacket pocket, with a single earpiece jack and a minimal control surface. Its reputation in the field is excellent among anyone who needs to stay reachable without staying locatable, and Tessera's decision to offer a consumer-licensed version (with reduced hop frequency and mandatory registration) has only deepened the market for unlicensed units with the full drift capability intact.

specifications.dimensions: 13cm x 6cm x 1.8cm wrist-mount or pocket form
specifications.hop_frequency: Every 4.3 seconds (unlicensed); every 30 seconds (licensed consumer version)
specifications.urban_coverage: Functional in any district with mesh node density above 40 nodes/km²
specifications.output: Standard encrypted voice and text; compatible with most mesh-capable devices

tactical_use: Worn during active operations where maintaining communication without creating a locatable signature is essential. Particularly effective in urban chase scenarios — a runner can stay in contact with support teams without broadcasting a traceable position. Also used by handlers who need to direct field assets without exposing their own location. The latency overhead is negligible for voice and text but makes it unsuitable for real-time data-heavy applications.
cultural_context: The PAS occupies a peculiar legal gray zone in GLMZ — the licensed version is sold openly in electronics markets and is popular among journalists, lawyers, and privacy-conscious citizens. The unlicensed full-drift version is technically a restricted device but is so visually identical to the licensed model that enforcement is inconsistent. Tessera has been accused, credibly, of deliberately engineering this ambiguity to maintain plausible deniability while flooding the market with devices their own security arm relies on.
known_users: Anyone who needs to stay reachable but not findable
story_hooks: A PAS unit is transmitting from somewhere in the city on a loop — same message, cycling through thousands of nodes. Someone set it going and never came back to turn it off.
The players are given a PAS unit by a contact who immediately disappears. The unit keeps receiving incoming calls from a number that doesn't resolve to any registered identity.

Tessera's address drift algorithm has developed an unexpected behavior in GLMZ's current mesh configuration — certain routing paths keep recurring, and someone has figured out how to predict where a PAS user will route next.

A licensed PAS unit was used in a high-profile assassination. The investigators want the players to prove it was unlicensed — or confirm that the licensed version is capable of the same anonymity Tessera claims only the black-market version provides.
